title: Italy with Lino Patruno, Monte Carlo, Norway and Scotland
summary: He plays with a television-star guitarist in Italy, Monte Carlo for IBM, Norway and Scotland, finding bands that play his style except one two-beat group.

bands.name: Pa Pa Bue's Viking Jazz Band

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: life. And, of course, you know, I played in Italy - I played with Nino Protruno's band and he is T.V. star ---

I call him Lini Patrinì but that's the best I can do -- but anyway, here again, I ran into a hell of a band; I've recorded with them twice; made a long playing album and, uh, he is a T.V. star; he is a comedian, a T.V. star; he is a movie star; he is the best guitar player--- one of the best guitar players and he sings and all this stuff and you walk down the street with this guy - and everybody says -oh, there's Leno - you know - they point him out on the street. Everybody knows him.
(inaudible) Play the guitar - what kind of style--
-- Barney Kessel? Those kind of guys.

Yes - big band guitar - really marvelous. And, I've been there three times and then I went to Monte Carlo with the Pa Pa Bue Band and we did a great big thing for IBM and they put us up in the best hotel in town; we played three days there; so - you see - over there, I just keep going. I play Norway - I just came back.

Just on this last little tour - I played Norway before I went to England and a very good band there as well and, uh, of course - always good bands in Scotland. There are more damn good jazz players in Scotland; they play clarinets and tenors and-- very good bands.
I'm going to have to try to see if I can get you to find somebody who didn't play well over there---

Well, look - they don't all do it but I say this - I say this - in all these bands, from six-piece bands mostly - sometimes seven, they use a four rhythm section with a guitar - there's always three or four very outstanding musicians in these groups. So, you see, what they do - they get the best they got in those towns that I play that play my style and it wa only on one occasion that I got with a band that played George Lewis style and I must say -- it was a two beat rhythm section; I was lost for that night. I couldn't get the band off the ground. And, of course, you know my Switzerland thing. But, I've named 17 - 18 countries here--
